name: @kineticist/mcp-server

tools.name: search_pinball_games
tools.description: Find pinball machines: "what Stern machines are in production right now?", "what pinball games has Stern made?", "pinball games from 1992". `in_production` filters to machines Kineticist lists as currently made. Searches and filters the Kineticist pinball game database. Supports text search, manufacturer filtering, year ranges, production status, and sorting. Returns game names, slugs, manufacturers, fun scores, edition counts, and each game's page URL on kineticist.com (link it when citing a game). `newest_edition_year` is the year the newest edition came out, not the year production ended; `in_production` says whether the game is still made.

q.description: Text search by game name (fuzzy, 2+ chars). Natural language works — 'that stern game with dinosaurs' will find Godzilla.

manufacturer.description: Filter by manufacturer name or slug (fuzzy match — 'stern' works)

in_production.description: Filter to only games currently in production (true) or out of production (false)

sort.description: Sort field. Prefix with - for descending. Options: name, first_manufacture_year, average_fun_score, ratings_count

tools.name: get_game_details
tools.description: Price, production status and details of a pinball machine: "how much is the Godzilla Premium, and is it still made?", "how much is the Jurassic Park Premium?", "what is Godzilla pinball?". Includes each edition's list price (MSRP) and whether the machine is in production. Full details for one game including editions (Pro/Premium/LE with pricing), images, tags, description, and rules links. `url` is the game's page on kineticist.com (link it when citing); remakes carry their own `url`. Editions that belong to a remake are listed under that remake. `best_image` (when present) is the one picture to show for the game: its URL, what it shows (backglass, photo, cabinet, flyer or playfield) and its size. Accepts slug (godzilla-2021), OPDB group ID (weeP), or OPDB machine ID (GweeP-MW95j). Use ?include=credits to also get the design team. `newest_edition_year` is the year the newest edition came out, not the year production ended; `in_production` says whether the game is still made.

id.description: Game slug, OPDB ID, or Kineticist game ID

include_credits.description: Include design team credits (designer, artist, programmer, etc.)

tools.name: get_random_game
tools.description: Suggest a pinball machine: "surprise me", "pinball game of the day". A random pinball game with full details, including `best_image` (the one picture to show) when there is one. Different game every time.

tools.name: get_pinball_stats
tools.description: How big is the pinball world: "how many pinball machines are in production?", "how many pinball manufacturers are there?". Kineticist database statistics: total games, games in production, total manufacturers, total designers, average fun score, most rated game, and newest game.

tools.name: get_game_credits
tools.description: Who designed a pinball machine: "who designed Medieval Madness?", "who designed Attack from Mars?", "who did the art for Twilight Zone?". Returns the full credited team, not just the lead designer. The design team for a pinball game — designer, artist, programmer, mechanical engineer, sound designer, animator, etc. Each credit includes the person's name and role. Every row carries `role` (slug, e.g. "design"), `role_name` (display name, e.g. "Design"), and, only where several people share a role on the game, `is_lead: true` on the first chair (no is_lead means no ranking, not "not the lead"). Read `role_name` for human display; `role` is the stable slug for filtering. Each person carries `url`, their page on kineticist.com, and `game_url` is the game's page (link them when citing).

tools.name: list_game_files
tools.description: Find a pinball manual or schematic: "where's the Firepower manual?", "schematics for Fish Tales". Lists a pinball game's downloadable files (manuals, ROMs, schematics, parts lists, bulletins) grouped by the machine each file is for. Each file line ends with a one-line description of what sets it apart (edition, print, language, format) when the title alone doesn't say. Use it to answer 'which file is for which machine' — e.g. Firepower's page also carries Taito's Fire Action files, and this tool tells them apart. Pass `machine` (trm_ id, slug, UUID or OPDB machine id) to narrow to one machine. Lists metadata only and ends with the game page's Documentation link; downloading a file needs a free Kineticist account on that page.

machine.description: Optional machine filter: trm_ id, slug, UUID or OPDB machine id

tools.name: where_to_play
tools.description: Where to play pinball, or a specific machine: "where can I play Godzilla near 97214?", "where can I play pinball in Chicago?", "pinball bars in Portland". Finds pinball venues near a place: a postal code ("60601", "SW1A 1AA" with country gb) or a city ("Chicago", "Portland, OR"). Pass `game` (name or slug) to find venues that have that machine. Returns up to 10 venues, nearest first, with city, distance in miles, machine count, venue kind (bar, arcade…) and `url`, the venue's page on kineticist.com (link it; it has the address and full machine list). `searched` says which place distances are measured from ("central Chicago, IL" is the city centre; "(middle of our venues there)" means a smaller city placed by its venues); `note` says when these are the nearest anywhere rather than nearby. Machine lists come from Pinball Map and can lag.

place.description: Postal code or city, e.g. "60601", "Chicago", "Portland, OR"

country.description: Two-letter country code for postal codes outside the US (gb, ca, de…). Default us.

game.description: Only venues that have this game: a name ("Godzilla") or slug (godzilla-2021)

tools.name: search
tools.description: Look up anything pinball on Kineticist: "who is Steve Ritchie?", "tell me about Spooky Pinball", "Kineticist articles about Pinburgh". Searches everything on Kineticist: games, news articles, places to play, manufacturers, people, mods, Hype Index entries and creators. Returns up to 10 matches, best first, each with its type, title, a short subtitle and `url` (its page on kineticist.com). Pass `type` to look in one kind only. For game details use get_game_details; for any other result, pass its url to `get`.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. "Steve Ritchie", "Stern", "Pinburgh"

tools.name: get
tools.description: Read what Kineticist says about something: "what does Kineticist say about Logan Arcade?", or any www.kineticist.com link. Reads a Kineticist page by its link, as markdown: a game, Hype Index entry, place to play, manufacturer, person, mod or creator. News articles come back as headline, date, summary and link only; the full article is at the link. Use the `url` from search or another tool.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: What's new in pinball: "what's new in pinball this week?", "latest pinball news", "what's climbing the Hype Index?". The latest Kineticist news articles (headline, date, summary and link; `members_section` means part of the article is for members; `games` lists the machines an article covers, get_game_details with a game's slug returns its editions, prices and design team; a release announced in the last few days may not have its new editions in the database yet, so check the edition dates against the article before quoting prices), new videos, podcasts and posts from the pinball creators Kineticist follows (`from_creators`: title, creator, format, date, summary, link), and Kineticist's Hype Index ranking (the current top 10 and this week's biggest climbers; `change_this_week` and `up` are places moved on the index since a week ago, positive is up, and a missing change means there's no rank from a week ago). This covers the week in pinball; each article and creator item carries its link.

days.description: How far back to look for news, in days (default 7)

tools.name: kineticist_log_play
tools.description: Log a play of a pinball game for the authenticated user. Use get_game_details first if you only have a slug — this tool needs the id from that response. playedAt must be today or earlier; at most 20 plays per game per day are accepted. Set dateKnown=false when the user has played the game but doesn't remember when or where; the diary will render "at some point". Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

gameId.description: Game UUID. Accepts both the raw UUID and the 'gm_'-prefixed form that get_game_details returns (prefix stripped automatically).

playedAt.description: Play date, YYYY-MM-DD. Must be today or earlier. Still required when dateKnown is false — send today's date as a placeholder.

dateKnown.description: Defaults to true. Set to false when the play is a vague 'I played this at some point' claim with no real date.

locationText.description: Freeform location name if locationId is unknown

score.description: Score on the machine, not a fun rating

isReplay.description: Flag as a replay rather than first-time play

tools.name: kineticist_toggle_ownership
tools.description: Mark a game as owned ("own") or no longer owned ("disown") for the authenticated user. The website treats this as toggle-like — calling "own" twice will error on the second call because the first ownership record is still open. Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

gameId.description: Game UUID. Accepts both the raw UUID and the 'gm_'-prefixed form that get_game_details returns (prefix stripped automatically).

removedAt.description: ISO date, YYYY-MM-DD. Only meaningful when action is 'disown'. Must be today or earlier.

annotations.title: Mark a game owned or not owned

tools.name: kineticist_toggle_want
tools.description: Toggle the authenticated user's want-to-play or want-to-own flag for a game. Calling twice turns the flag back off. Logging a play or marking the game owned will auto-clear the matching want flag server-side. Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

gameId.description: Game UUID. Accepts both the raw UUID and the 'gm_'-prefixed form that get_game_details returns (prefix stripped automatically).

wantType.description: 'play' toggles the want-to-play list; 'own' toggles the wishlist

annotations.title: Toggle want to play or own

tools.name: kineticist_set_fun_score
tools.description: Set the authenticated user's fun score (1-100) for a game. Upserts — calling again overwrites. Also updates the score attached to any existing written review. Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

gameId.description: Game UUID. Accepts both the raw UUID and the 'gm_'-prefixed form that get_game_details returns (prefix stripped automatically).

tools.name: kineticist_undo_last_play
tools.description: Delete the authenticated user's most recent play log for a game. Walks played_at then created_at descending. Errors if there is no play to undo. Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

gameId.description: Game UUID. Accepts both the raw UUID and the 'gm_'-prefixed form that get_game_details returns (prefix stripped automatically).

tools.name: kineticist_toggle_favorite
tools.description: Toggle the authenticated user's favorite/follow. Provide gameId to favorite a game, or promoterId or promoterSlug to follow a creator (the same Following list the /promoters Following tab reads). promoterSlug is the last part of a creator's page url (https://www.kineticist.com/promoters/{slug}). Calling twice removes it. Returns { success, favorited }. Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

gameId.description: Game UUID. Accepts both the raw UUID and the 'gm_'-prefixed form that get_game_details returns (prefix stripped automatically).

promoterId.description: Kineticist promoter (creator) UUID to follow/unfollow. Provide one of gameId, promoterId or promoterSlug.

promoterSlug.description: Creator slug, the last part of its page url. Used when you have the creator's page but not its UUID.

annotations.title: Favorite a game or follow a creator

tools.name: kineticist_delete_fun_score
tools.description: Delete the authenticated user's fun score for a game. Errors if no score exists. The fun score recorded inside a written review is NOT removed by this — call kineticist_delete_review for that. Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

gameId.description: Game UUID. Accepts both the raw UUID and the 'gm_'-prefixed form that get_game_details returns (prefix stripped automatically).

tools.name: kineticist_update_play_log
tools.description: Update an existing play log row owned by the authenticated user. Use the play log id from a prior list — these are NOT game ids. playedAt must be today or earlier. Pass any subset of fields to update; omitted fields are left untouched. Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

playLogId.description: Play log row UUID to update — not a game id.

playedAt.description: Play date, YYYY-MM-DD. Must be today or earlier.

score.description: Score on the machine, not a fun rating.

tools.name: kineticist_delete_play_log
tools.description: Delete an existing play log row owned by the authenticated user. Use the play log id from a prior list — these are NOT game ids. Decrements the game's plays_count via the same DB trigger that powers undo_last_play. Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

playLogId.description: Play log row UUID to delete — not a game id.

tools.name: kineticist_update_ownership_details
tools.description: Update the rich detail on the authenticated user's most-recent open ownership record for a game (purchase price, source, trade detail, trim, sale price). The user must currently own the game. Pass any subset of fields; omitted fields are left untouched. Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

gameId.description: Game UUID. Accepts both the raw UUID and the 'gm_'-prefixed form that get_game_details returns (prefix stripped automatically).

salePrice.description: USD. Only meaningful for previously-owned (closed) records.

tools.name: kineticist_submit_review
tools.description: Save the authenticated user's review (fun score 1-100 + optional written body) for a game. Upserts on (game, user). The score is the same one kineticist_set_fun_score touches; submitting a review with score keeps both surfaces aligned. Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

gameId.description: Game UUID. Accepts both the raw UUID and the 'gm_'-prefixed form that get_game_details returns (prefix stripped automatically).

body.description: Optional written review. Omit or empty string for score-only.

tools.name: kineticist_delete_review
tools.description: Delete the authenticated user's review for a game. Errors if the user has no review on this game. The fun score recorded via kineticist_set_fun_score is NOT removed by this — call kineticist_delete_fun_score for that. Acts on the API key owner's own library. Available on every tier, but agents that make many calls per task burn through a free-tier daily quota quickly. Email colin@kineticist.com for a higher ceiling.

gameId.description: Game UUID. Accepts both the raw UUID and the 'gm_'-prefixed form that get_game_details returns (prefix stripped automatically).

tools.name: kineticist_get_my_state
tools.description: Get the authenticated user's engagement state for a game: owned, wishlist flags, play count, latest play, fun score, ownership details (trim, purchase price, acquired/removed dates). Read-only. Use after a write tool to verify.

gameId.description: Game UUID. Accepts both the raw UUID and the 'gm_'-prefixed form that get_game_details returns (prefix stripped automatically).

annotations.title: Get your status for a game

instructions:
Kineticist (kineticist.com) is a pinball publication and database. These tools cover pinball machines and their editions, list prices (MSRP) and production status; design credits; places to play near a postal code or city, and which venues have a given machine; manufacturers, designers and other people; recent pinball news and creator videos; and Kineticist's Hype Index of pinball themes.

Which tool: where_to_play for places to play; whats_new for recent pinball news, new videos and podcasts from pinball creators, and Hype Index moves; search_pinball_games and get_game_details for machines, their editions, prices and production status; get_game_credits for who designed a game; list_game_files for manuals and schematics; search for anything else on the site, then get to read a result's page.

Answers include kineticist.com page links (url); cite them when using Kineticist's data. News results are summaries, and the full story is at the article link.

A creator video or news tag can name a homebrew, another manufacturer's game or an unreleased one, so a game named there may not have its own entry in the database.

A game named with slashes, like "Family Guy / Shrek", is one playfield sold under several themes, grouped on purpose.

Tools starting with kineticist_ act on the API key owner's own Kineticist library (plays, ownership, wishlist, fun scores, reviews).
